land.cliopatria: French Mandate for Syria and Lebanon
land.text: Syria as the mandate left it after Lebanon was separated: independence 'attained on 24 October 1945' and the last French troops out on 17 April 1946

predecessors.note: The page also says Syria was recognised as an independent republic on 1 January 1944 (text) and gives 17 April 1946 as independence (infobox). Cliopatria's mandate row covers Syria alone in 1944-1945.

land.text: Syria as the Northern region of the union with Egypt announced on 1 February 1958; infobox formation 22 February 1958

successors.note: The Second Republic was restored in 1961 after the Syrian coup of 28 September 1961 (UAR page), which Cliopatria records as Republic of Syria 1961-1962.

keyframe_review.note: 186,281 km2 against the infobox 189,880 km2 (ratio 0.98); with the five cells about 187,580 km2 (ratio 0.99). Adjusted: the 1946 outline lacks the Golan edge that Cliopatria adds in 1949, but the Golan page puts the Golan in French Syria from the 1923 boundary and in independent Syria afterwards, so the land was Syrian throughout and the 1949 cells are not a new gain. Cells added: 33.23N 35.83E and 32.44N 36.37E (inside Natural Earth's Syria) and 33.10N 35.71E, 32.95N 35.78E, 32.82N 35.66E (the gazetteer's Golan region), about 1,300 km2 in all. The Second Syrian Republic page: independence on 17 April 1946, 'when France withdrew its last troops', frontiers the mandate's; in 1936 the treaty with France had Jabal Druze and the Alawite region join Syria, and in September 1938 France separated the Sanjak of Alexandretta (Turkey's Hatay in 1939), which Syria never recognised.

correction.text: Syria with the Golan edge it already had under the mandate: the Golan 'became part of French Syria' (Franco-British boundary agreement of December 1920, commission report approved 7 March 1923) and 'part of the newly independent state of Syria'; the five cells Cliopatria adds only in 1949 are drawn Syrian from the start

keyframe_review.note: 186,623 km2; with the five cells about 187,920 km2. Adjusted as for 1946: the Golan edge was Syrian under the mandate and through 1948 (Golan page), so the hatched 1948-1949 ground is drawn on Israeli land west of the border (see the ledger), not on these cells. Cells added: 33.23N 35.83E and 32.44N 36.37E (inside Natural Earth's Syria) and 33.10N 35.71E, 32.95N 35.78E, 32.82N 35.66E (the gazetteer's Golan region), about 1,300 km2 in all. Against 1946 the shape adds 5 cells and drops 2 in the eastern desert (33.6-35.8 N, 39.2-41.4 E); no event on the pages opened, so redrawing noise. The Second Syrian Republic page says Syria 'managed to keep their old borders and occupy some additional territory' ([citation needed]).

correction.text: Syria with the Golan edge it already had under the mandate: the Golan 'became part of French Syria' (Franco-British boundary agreement of December 1920, commission report approved 7 March 1923) and 'part of the newly independent state of Syria'; the five cells Cliopatria adds only in 1949 are drawn Syrian from the start

keyframe_review.note: 187,924 km2 (infobox 189,880 km2, ratio 0.99). The five cells it adds against 1948 (Golan and the south edge of the Syrian shape, 32.4-33.2 N, 35.7-36.4 E) are Syrian land east of the international border, not a border adjustment of the armistice of 20 July 1949: the 1946 and 1947 keyframes now carry them. The armistice page: Syria 'withdrew its forces from most of the territories it controlled west of the international border' and kept 66 km2 in the Jordan valley; that 66 km2 is below the 250 km2 cell size and is not drawn. The ground Syria left west of the border is drawn by the occupation_end of July 1949 on the Mishmar HaYarden cell.
No change in cells against 1949-1955. The page records martial law in Syria during the Suez crisis and a Turkish stand-off after the Soviet pact of November 1956, neither with a border change.

correction.text: the 1956 outline for 1958 until the union with Egypt in February 1958

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria ends this row in 1957 and starts its United Arab Republic row in 1958, but the union was announced on 1 February 1958 (infobox formation 22 February, referendum 21 February). January and part of February 1958 are drawn as the republic.

region.text: Syria, independent in 1946, with the Golan edge that was Syrian under the mandate (the same outline as the corrected 1946 keyframe)

ledger.note: 17 April 1946: Syria's independence, with the last French troops gone. Infobox 'Independence 17 April 1946'; the text has Syria recognised as independent on 1 January 1944 and 'Syrian independence was attained on 24 October 1945'. The land is the mandate's Syria, the page naming no boundary. The Cliopatria 1946 outline lacks five Golan and border cells it adds in 1949; they are added back here (Golan page: the Golan 'became part of French Syria').

region.text: the ground west of the international border that Syria fought for in 1948, drawn as the one cell around Mishmar HaYarden (33.00N 35.60E, the moshav's page coordinates 33.005N 35.599E), the place the page has the Syrians overrunning on 10 June; the lake-shore actions of 15-20 May (Ein Gev, Samakh, Degania) held no ground to the armistice and are not drawn. Not the Sea of Galilee, which the Golan Heights page says 'was placed entirely within British Mandatory Palestine', and not the Golan, which was Syrian

ledger.note: 15 May 1948: Syria invades Palestine. 'In the early hours of 15 May, the Syrian invasion began'; Ein Gev was attacked as a diversion, the Syrians took Samakh 'with a third attack on 18 May' and later left it, 'abandoning Samakh, Masada, and Sha'ar HaGolan', and attacked Degania on 20 May. The ground that stayed contested to the armistice is Mishmar HaYarden, west of the border, so the zone is drawn there; the shore fighting is below what the grid can show. The region is the author's reading (the page names no coordinates).

region.text: the ground west of the international border that Syria held from the overrunning of Mishmar HaYarden on 10 June 1948 until the armistice: 'The Israelis gained some ground but failed to dislodge the Syrians, who remained in the area until the 1949 armistice'. Drawn as the one cell around Mishmar HaYarden (33.00N 35.60E), the cell itself larger than the area

ledger.note: 10 June 1948: Syrian forces hold Mishmar HaYarden. 'On 6 June, Syrian forces attacked Mishmar HaYarden, but were repulsed. On 10 June, the Syrians overran Mishmar HaYarden in house-to-house fighting', then advanced to the main road, 'where they were stopped by units of the Oded Brigade'; the page's Operation Brosh passage adds that the Israelis 'failed to dislodge the Syrians, who remained in the area until the 1949 armistice'. The Second Syrian Republic page says Syria 'managed to keep their old borders and occupy some additional territory' (citation needed) while its army 'was pressed out of the Israeli areas, but fortified their strongholds on the Golan Heights'. The moshav's coordinates are from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mishmar_HaYarden.

region.text: the ground west of the international border that Syria held from the overrunning of Mishmar HaYarden on 10 June 1948 until the armistice: 'The Israelis gained some ground but failed to dislodge the Syrians, who remained in the area until the 1949 armistice'. Drawn as the one cell around Mishmar HaYarden (33.00N 35.60E), the cell itself larger than the area

ledger.note: 20 July 1949: the Syrian armistice. Syria 'withdrew its forces from most of the territories it controlled west of the international border' (the areas became demilitarised zones under Syrian control) and kept 66 km2 in the Jordan valley; Syria 'was the last Arab country to sign an armistice agreement with Israel' and Article V says the line has no bearing on 'ultimate territorial arrangements'. The 66 km2 Syria kept in the Jordan valley is below cell size and the DMZs are not drawn separately; the cell drawn here is the ground Syria held at Mishmar HaYarden.

region.text: the ground west of the international border that Syria fought for in 1948, drawn as the one cell around Mishmar HaYarden (33.00N 35.60E, the moshav's page coordinates 33.005N 35.599E), the place the page has the Syrians overrunning on 10 June; the lake-shore actions of 15-20 May (Ein Gev, Samakh, Degania) held no ground to the armistice and are not drawn. Not the Sea of Galilee, which the Golan Heights page says 'was placed entirely within British Mandatory Palestine', and not the Golan, which was Syrian

ledger.note: 20 July 1949: Syria and Israel sign the armistice, ending the fighting on the Syrian front; Israel had signed with Egypt on 24 February, Lebanon on 23 March and Jordan on 3 April. The zone is the Mishmar HaYarden cell of the occupation pair.

region.text: Syria, now the northern region of the United Arab Republic

ledger.note: 1 February 1958: Syria and Egypt announce their union as the United Arab Republic. Kuwatli and Nasser 'announced the merging of the two countries' on 1 February 1958 (Second Syrian Republic page); referendums followed on 21 February and the infobox gives formation on 22 February 1958; the capital is Cairo. Syria seceded on 28 September 1961.

wars.name: 1948 Arab-Israeli War (Syrian front)

zones.text: the ground west of the international border that Syria fought for in 1948, drawn as the one cell around Mishmar HaYarden (33.00N 35.60E, the moshav's page coordinates 33.005N 35.599E), the place the page has the Syrians overrunning on 10 June; the lake-shore actions of 15-20 May (Ein Gev, Samakh, Degania) held no ground to the armistice and are not drawn. Not the Sea of Galilee, which the Golan Heights page says 'was placed entirely within British Mandatory Palestine', and not the Golan, which was Syrian

wars.outcome: Syria invaded on 15 May 1948, took Samakh (18 May) and left it, attacked Degania (20 May), overran Mishmar HaYarden (10 June) and was 'stopped just west of the original border between Palestine and Syria'; the Syrians 'remained in the area until the 1949 armistice' (20 July 1949), when Syria withdrew from most ground west of the international border, keeping 66 km2 and the demilitarised zones.
wars.note: Page read in full (characters 0-122,137) on a second pass. The zone is one cell at Mishmar HaYarden, the only place west of the border the page has Syria holding to the armistice.

certainty.note: Frontiers inherited from the mandate; the eastern desert frontier is approximate and the Sanjak of Alexandretta, lost to Turkey in 1939, was never recognised.

The Israeli frontier is the armistice line of 20 July 1949, a line along the international border with demilitarised zones; the eastern desert frontier with Iraq and Jordan stays approximate and Hatay is still claimed.

notes: Cliopatria's Second Syrian Republic row is 1946-1957 and the union with Egypt is in its United Arab Republic row from 1958; this dossier ends the republic in February 1958 (the page's date for the union announcement), so its January-February 1958 keyframe overlaps Cliopatria's first UAR year. The page's infobox formation date for the UAR is 22 February 1958; the text says 1 February. The 1947 change of a few cells in the eastern desert has no dated event on the pages opened. The five cells Cliopatria adds in 1949 (Golan and the Syrian edge) are Syrian land under the mandate and are added to the 1946 and 1947 keyframes; the 1948-1949 occupation and contest are drawn as one cell around Mishmar HaYarden, west of the border (repaired after review; the first draft drew the Sea of Galilee and these cells). Not read within the page budget: the Syrian-Iraqi and Syrian-Jordanian frontier details, the evacuation of French troops in 1945-1946 (the Levant crisis), the demilitarised zone disputes of 1951-1956, the 1957 Turkish crisis (the page gives it no date), and the Syrian Desert frontier. The page's presidents list in the infobox is garbled (it mixes the First and Second Republics), so no ruler strip is given. Needs no new dossier; the Sanjak of Alexandretta (Hatay), lost in 1939, belongs to the French mandate and Turkey dossiers.
